questions.q: What is the grain of dw.FactProductSales in this capstone's star schema?
options: One row per order line (one row per Sales.SalesOrderDetail record)
One row per customer
One row per sales territory
One row per calendar quarter
questions.explain: The grain is fixed first, at one row per order line, and every column added to the fact table has to be true at that grain.

questions.q: Why does dw.DimProduct flatten CategoryName and SubcategoryName directly onto itself instead of using separate dimension tables for category and subcategory?
options: Because Production.ProductCategory doesn't really exist in AdventureWorks2012
So every front-end gets the category resolved once, during the warehouse load, instead of each one re-running the same two-table join itself
Because Tableau cannot join more than one dimension table
Because flattening is required for Power BI relationships to work at all
questions.explain: Resolving the Product → ProductSubcategory → ProductCategory join once during the load means every one of the three front-ends gets one simple, already-flattened dimension table.

questions.q: Why are Sales.Customer.PersonID and StoreID both modeled as nullable on dw.DimCustomer?
options: Because the warehouse load is incomplete
Because a real AdventureWorks2012 customer is either an individual person or a store account, never both, so one of the two columns is always null
Because PersonID and StoreID are deprecated columns
Because Finance requested they be hidden
questions.explain: In the real source data, a customer row has exactly one of PersonID or StoreID populated — the warehouse carries that real distinction forward honestly instead of papering over it.

questions.q: Why can't dw.FactProductSales's foreign-key constraints be declared the moment the fact table itself is created?
options: Because SQL Server does not support foreign keys on fact tables
Because the dimension tables those constraints would reference don't exist yet at that point in the build
Because foreign keys are only allowed on dimension tables, never fact tables
Because the measures haven't been calculated yet
questions.explain: A REFERENCES constraint against a table that doesn't exist yet fails in SQL Server, so the fact table's columns are defined first and the constraints are added later, once the dimensions exist and are populated.

questions.q: Which real AdventureWorks2012 source table supplies the TerritoryID used to build dw.DimTerritory?
options: Production.Product
Sales.SalesOrderHeader
Sales.SalesTerritory
Production.ProductCategory
questions.explain: Sales.SalesTerritory supplies TerritoryID, Name, and Group — the real source columns dw.DimTerritory is built from.
